newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Opposition aims for second minister.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Opposition aims for second minister.

text.p: The Australian Opposition took aim at a second minister on Monday after taking the scalp of former assistant treasurer Jim Short, who resigned on the weekend after it was found that he improperly held bank shares.
Opposition industry spokesman Simon Crean said in Parliament that Industry Minister John Moore also held shares in a company connected to his portfolio.

"Minister, your most recent declaration of registerable interests shows that ... you still own shares in a company named Bligh Ventures, a venture capital company with substantial interests in the petroleum industry, in computer
technology, in agricultural research and development and in telecommunications," Crean said.
Moore replied that he still held the shares because, although he had put them up for sale the market for them was illiquid.
Short, who held shares in Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, was a junior minister in the treasury portfolio, which is responsible for the banking industry.
Although he and Prime Minister John Howard initially resisted pressure for him to resign, he quit on Sunday after his office discovered that he had approved a banking license for an ANZ subsidiary.
